agree.reason: The signed records, the two clean state audits and the 20-to-12-hour rewrite speak directly to a skeptic who assumes teachers don't understand regulated work, so a phone screen is likely, though the unaddressed LMS gap and missing start date leave her with open questions.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unprovable promise to halve training time and keeps every figure true to the facts, though saying the lab safety record has held since the 2020 change is a slight inference from the injury record.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are restated rather than worked: it never calls the 20-to-12 change a 40% cut, never totals the hours saved across about two new teachers a year, and never counts the signed records kept over seven years.

right_comparison.reason: It honestly compares the old 20-hour training with the new 12-hour version and the AP pass rate rising from 41% to 58%, and it sensibly proposes measuring the plant's own baseline rather than inventing one.

qualification.reason: The GMP gap is hedged with a checkable date (May 2), but the letter leaves out the June 14 earliest start, which HR needs to know, and gives no consequence or interview availability.

objections.reason: The regulated-industry and GMP-records objections are met well with audit-ready signed records and the enrolled course, but her unfamiliarity with the plant's learning management system goes unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted one-page cover letter addressed to the named HR manager, though the applicant's name is left as a placeholder.
